fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Garden Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responding units can identify it as the only access point without searching.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear dense vegetation back from the sides of the main residence to allow responders to move around the building on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can reach both buildings and move between them.
• Cut back any branches or shrubs that hang over or press against either structure.
• Keep the perimeter fencing gate closest to the rear of the property unlocked or fitted with a breakaway latch to allow responders to reach the rear without going back to the front.
• Mark any gate locations on the perimeter fence with reflective indicators so responders can find them quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the walkway clear of overgrown plantings from the landscaped area so responders can move along it without detours.
• Identify a flat, open staging area near the access drive where emergency vehicles can park and crews can work without blocking the driveway.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored items, equipment, or debris that would reduce the space available for responder staging.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Along Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees that overhang or touch the house on any side.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the house.
• Clear overhanging branches along the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles.
• Trim back shrubs and low branches along both sides of the driveway edge.
• Remove dead wood and dry plant material from under scattered trees near the house.
• Cut back any shrubs or low tree branches that connect ground-level plants to the lower branches of larger trees.
• Keep the area immediately around the structure clear of loose plant material, dry leaves, and fallen branches.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the property as much as possible to reduce the limited access problem from that side.
• Separate shrub groupings from nearby trees by removing plants that bridge the gap between them.
